verses.raw: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
verses.text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.

verses.raw: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that comes after the king? even that which has been already done.
verses.text: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that comes after the king? even that which has been already done.

verses.raw: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
verses.text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.

verses.raw: The wise man’s eyes are in his head; but the fool walks in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
verses.text: The wise man’s eyes are in his head; but the fool walks in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

verses.raw: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
verses.text: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.

verses.raw: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dies the wise man? as the fool.
verses.text: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dies the wise man? as the fool.

verses.raw: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.text: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.raw: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
verses.text: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.

verses.raw: And who knows whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.
verses.text: And who knows whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.

verses.raw: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.
verses.text: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.

verses.raw: For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that has not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.text: For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that has not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.

verses.raw: For what has man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he has laboured under the sun?
verses.text: For what has man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he has laboured under the sun?

verses.raw: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart takes not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
verses.text: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart takes not rest in the night. This is also vanity.

verses.raw: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of Elohim (God).
verses.text: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of Elohim.

verses.raw: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?
verses.text: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?

verses.raw: For Elohim (God) gives to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before Elohim (God). This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.text: For Elohim gives to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before Elohim. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.raw: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
verses.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

verses.raw: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
verses.text: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;

verses.raw: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.text: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

verses.raw: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

verses.raw: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.text: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

verses.raw: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
verses.text: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

verses.raw: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

verses.raw: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
verses.text: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

verses.raw: What profit has he that works in that wherein he laboureth?
verses.text: What profit has he that works in that wherein he laboureth?

verses.raw: I have seen the travail, which Elohim (God) has given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
verses.text: I have seen the travail, which Elohim has given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.

verses.raw: He has made every thing beautiful in his time: also he has set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that Elohim (God) makes from the beginning to the end.
verses.text: He has made every thing beautiful in his time: also he has set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that Elohim makes from the beginning to the end.

verses.raw: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
verses.text: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

verses.raw: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of Elohim (God).
verses.text: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of Elohim.

verses.raw: I know that, whatsoever Elohim (God) does, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and Elohim (God) does it, that men should fear before him.
verses.text: I know that, whatsoever Elohim does, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and Elohim does it, that men should fear before him.

verses.raw: That which has been is now; and that which is to be has already been; and Elohim (God) requires that which is past.
verses.text: That which has been is now; and that which is to be has already been; and Elohim requires that which is past.

verses.raw: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
verses.text: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.

verses.raw: I said in my heart, Elohim (God) shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
verses.text: I said in my heart, Elohim shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.

verses.raw: I said in my heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that Elohim (God) might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.
verses.text: I said in my heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that Elohim might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.

verses.raw: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dies, so dies the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man has no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
verses.text: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dies, so dies the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man has no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.

verses.raw: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
verses.text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.

verses.raw: Who knows the spirit of man that goes upward, and the spirit of the beast that goes downward to the earth?
verses.text: Who knows the spirit of man that goes upward, and the spirit of the beast that goes downward to the earth?

verses.raw: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
verses.text: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

verses.raw: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
verses.text: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.

verses.raw: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
verses.text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

verses.raw: Yea, better is he than both they, which has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.text: Yea, better is he than both they, which has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

verses.raw: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.text: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.raw: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eats his own flesh.
verses.text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eats his own flesh.

verses.raw: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.
verses.text: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

verses.raw: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
verses.text: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.

verses.raw: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he has neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither says he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.
verses.text: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he has neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither says he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.

verses.raw: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
verses.text: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

verses.raw: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls; for he has not another to help him up.
verses.text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls; for he has not another to help him up.

verses.raw: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
verses.text: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?

verses.raw: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

verses.raw: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
verses.text: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.

verses.raw: For out of prison he comes to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becomes poor.
verses.text: For out of prison he comes to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becomes poor.

verses.raw: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
verses.text: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.

verses.raw: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.text: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.raw: Keep your foot when you go to the house of Elohim (God), and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
verses.text: Keep your foot when you go to the house of Elohim, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.

verses.raw: Be not rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be hasty to utter any thing before Elohim (God): for Elohim (God) is in heaven, and you upon earth: therefore let your words be few.
verses.text: Be not rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be hasty to utter any thing before Elohim: for Elohim is in heaven, and you upon earth: therefore let your words be few.

verses.raw: For a dream comes through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.
verses.text: For a dream comes through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.

verses.raw: When you vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which you have vowed.
verses.text: When you vowest a vow unto Elohim, defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which you have vowed.

verses.raw: Better is it that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
verses.text: Better is it that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.

verses.raw: Suffer not your mouth to cause your flesh to sin; neither say you before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should Elohim (God) be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.text: Suffer not your mouth to cause your flesh to sin; neither say you before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should Elohim be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?

verses.raw: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear you Elohim (God).
verses.text: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear you Elohim.

verses.raw: If you see the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regards; and there be higher than they.
verses.text: If you see the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regards; and there be higher than they.

verses.raw: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
verses.text: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.

verses.raw: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
verses.text: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.

verses.raw: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
verses.text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?

verses.raw: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
verses.text: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

verses.raw: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
verses.text: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.

verses.raw: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
verses.text: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.

verses.raw: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.text: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

verses.raw: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit has he that has laboured for the wind?
verses.text: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit has he that has laboured for the wind?

verses.raw: All his days also he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
verses.text: All his days also he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

verses.raw: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he takes under the sun all the days of his life, which Elohim (God) gives him: for it is his portion.
verses.text: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he takes under the sun all the days of his life, which Elohim gives him: for it is his portion.

verses.raw: Every man also to whom Elohim (God) has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of Elohim (God).
verses.text: Every man also to whom Elohim has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of Elohim.

verses.raw: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because Elohim (God) answers him in the joy of his heart.
verses.text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because Elohim answers him in the joy of his heart.

verses.raw: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
verses.text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:

verses.raw: A man to whom Elohim (God) has given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet Elohim (God) gives him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eats it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
verses.text: A man to whom Elohim has given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet Elohim gives him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eats it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

verses.raw: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
verses.text: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.

verses.raw: For he comes in with vanity, and departs in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
verses.text: For he comes in with vanity, and departs in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.

verses.raw: Moreover he has not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this has more rest than the other.
verses.text: Moreover he has not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this has more rest than the other.

verses.raw: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet has he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
verses.text: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet has he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

verses.raw: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.text: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

verses.raw: For what has the wise more than the fool? what has the poor, that knows to walk before the living?
verses.text: For what has the wise more than the fool? what has the poor, that knows to walk before the living?

verses.raw: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.text: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.raw: That which has been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
verses.text: That which has been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.

verses.raw: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
verses.text: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?

verses.raw: For who knows what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
verses.text: For who knows what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

verses.raw: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
verses.text: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

verses.raw: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
verses.text: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.

verses.raw: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
verses.text: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

verses.raw: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.

verses.raw: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

verses.raw: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
verses.text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.

verses.raw: Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; and a gift destroys the heart.
verses.text: Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; and a gift destroys the heart.

verses.raw: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.text: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.

verses.raw: Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
verses.text: Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.

verses.raw: Say not you, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for you do not enquire wisely concerning this.
verses.text: Say not you, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for you do not enquire wisely concerning this.

verses.raw: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
verses.text: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.

verses.raw: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom gives life to them that have it.
verses.text: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom gives life to them that have it.

verses.raw: Consider the work of Elohim (God): for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
verses.text: Consider the work of Elohim: for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?

verses.raw: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: Elohim (God) also has set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
verses.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: Elohim also has set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

verses.raw: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
verses.text: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.

verses.raw: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why should you destroy thyself?
verses.text: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why should you destroy thyself?

verses.raw: Be not over much wicked, neither be you foolish: why should you die before your time?
verses.text: Be not over much wicked, neither be you foolish: why should you die before your time?

verses.raw: It is good that you should take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not your hand: for he that fears Elohim (God) shall come forth of them all.
verses.text: It is good that you should take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not your hand: for he that fears Elohim shall come forth of them all.

verses.raw: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
verses.text: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.

verses.raw: For there is not a just man upon earth, that does good, and sins not.
verses.text: For there is not a just man upon earth, that does good, and sins not.

verses.raw: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest you hear your servant curse you:
verses.text: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest you hear your servant curse you:

verses.raw: For oftentimes also your own heart knows that you thyself likewise have cursed others.
verses.text: For oftentimes also your own heart knows that you thyself likewise have cursed others.

verses.raw: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
verses.text: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.

verses.raw: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
verses.text: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?

verses.raw: I applied my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
verses.text: I applied my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:

verses.raw: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth Elohim (God) shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
verses.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth Elohim shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

verses.raw: Behold, this have I found, says the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
verses.text: Behold, this have I found, says the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:

verses.raw: Which yet my soul seeks, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
verses.text: Which yet my soul seeks, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.

verses.raw: Lo, this only have I found, that Elohim (God) has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
verses.text: Lo, this only have I found, that Elohim has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.

verses.raw: Who is as the wise man? and who knows the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
verses.text: Who is as the wise man? and who knows the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

verses.raw: I counsel you to keep the king’s commandment, and that in regard of the oath of Elohim (God).
verses.text: I counsel you to keep the king’s commandment, and that in regard of the oath of Elohim.

verses.raw: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he does whatsoever pleaseth him.
verses.text: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he does whatsoever pleaseth him.

verses.raw: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What do you?
verses.text: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What do you?

verses.raw: Whoso keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.
verses.text: Whoso keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.

verses.raw: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.
verses.text: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.

verses.raw: For he knows not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
verses.text: For he knows not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?

verses.raw: There is no man that has power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither has he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
verses.text: There is no man that has power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither has he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.

verses.raw: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man rules over another to his own hurt.
verses.text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man rules over another to his own hurt.

verses.raw: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.
verses.text: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.

verses.raw: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

verses.raw: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear Elohim (God), which fear before him:
verses.text: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear Elohim, which fear before him:

verses.raw: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he fears not before Elohim (God).
verses.text: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he fears not before Elohim.

verses.raw: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
verses.text: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.

verses.raw: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which Elohim (God) gives him under the sun.
verses.text: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which Elohim gives him under the sun.

verses.raw: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes:)
verses.text: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes:)

verses.raw: Then I beheld all the work of Elohim (God), that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
verses.text: Then I beheld all the work of Elohim, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.

verses.raw: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of Elohim (God): no man knows either love or hatred by all that is before them.
verses.text: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of Elohim: no man knows either love or hatred by all that is before them.

verses.raw: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that swears, as he that fears an oath.
verses.text: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that swears, as he that fears an oath.

verses.raw: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
verses.text: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.

verses.raw: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.text: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

verses.raw: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

verses.raw: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
verses.text: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.

verses.raw: Go your way, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for Elohim (God) now accepts your works.
verses.text: Go your way, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for Elohim now accepts your works.

verses.raw: Let your garments be always white; and let your head lack no ointment.
verses.text: Let your garments be always white; and let your head lack no ointment.

verses.raw: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of the life of your vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity: for that is your portion in this life, and in your labour which you take under the sun.
verses.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of the life of your vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity: for that is your portion in this life, and in your labour which you take under the sun.

verses.raw: Whatsoever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither you go.
verses.text: Whatsoever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither you go.

verses.raw: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
verses.text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

verses.raw: For man also knows not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them.
verses.text: For man also knows not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them.

verses.raw: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me:
verses.text: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me:

verses.raw: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
verses.text: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

verses.raw: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
verses.text: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.

verses.raw: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
verses.text: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.

verses.raw: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that rules among fools.
verses.text: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that rules among fools.

verses.raw: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroys much good.

verses.raw: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so does a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
verses.text: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so does a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.

verses.raw: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.text: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.

verses.raw: Yea also, when he that is a fool walks by the way, his wisdom fails him, and he says to every one that he is a fool.
verses.text: Yea also, when he that is a fool walks by the way, his wisdom fails him, and he says to every one that he is a fool.

verses.raw: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against you, leave not your place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
verses.text: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against you, leave not your place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.

verses.raw: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceeds from the ruler:
verses.text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceeds from the ruler:

verses.raw: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
verses.text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.

verses.raw: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
verses.text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.

verses.raw: He that digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaks an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.text: He that digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaks an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

verses.raw: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaves wood shall be endangered thereby.
verses.text: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaves wood shall be endangered thereby.

verses.raw: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
verses.text: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.

verses.raw: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
verses.text: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.

verses.raw: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
verses.text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

verses.raw: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
verses.text: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

verses.raw: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.text: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

verses.raw: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knows not how to go to the city.
verses.text: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knows not how to go to the city.

verses.raw: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
verses.text: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!

verses.raw: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.text: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

verses.raw: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
verses.text: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.

verses.raw: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes merry: but money answers all things.
verses.text: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes merry: but money answers all things.

verses.raw: Curse not the king, no not in your thought; and curse not the rich in your bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.
verses.text: Curse not the king, no not in your thought; and curse not the rich in your bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.

verses.raw: Cast your bread upon the waters: for you shall find it after many days.
verses.text: Cast your bread upon the waters: for you shall find it after many days.

verses.raw: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for you know not what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for you know not what evil shall be upon the earth.

verses.raw: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall be.
verses.text: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall be.

verses.raw: He that observes the wind shall not sow; and he that regards the clouds shall not reap.
verses.text: He that observes the wind shall not sow; and he that regards the clouds shall not reap.

verses.raw: As you know not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so you know not the works of Elohim (God) who makes all.
verses.text: As you know not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so you know not the works of Elohim who makes all.

verses.raw: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening withhold not your hand: for you know not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
verses.text: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening withhold not your hand: for you know not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.

verses.raw: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
verses.text: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:

verses.raw: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
verses.text: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.

verses.raw: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth; and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes: but know you, that for all these things Elohim (God) will bring you into judgment.
verses.text: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth; and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes: but know you, that for all these things Elohim will bring you into judgment.

verses.raw: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
verses.text: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.

verses.raw: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when you shall say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.text: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when you shall say, I have no pleasure in them;

verses.raw: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
verses.text: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:

verses.raw: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
verses.text: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,

verses.raw: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
verses.text: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;

verses.raw: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goes to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
verses.text: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goes to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:

verses.raw: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
verses.text: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

verses.raw: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto Elohim (God) who gave it.
verses.text: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto Elohim who gave it.

verses.raw: Vanity of vanities, says the preacher; all is vanity.
verses.text: Vanity of vanities, says the preacher; all is vanity.

verses.raw: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.text: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

verses.raw: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
verses.text: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.

verses.raw: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
verses.text: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.

verses.raw: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.text: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

verses.raw: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

verses.raw: For Elohim (God) shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
verses.text: For Elohim shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

verses.raw: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
verses.text: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.

verses.raw: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for your love is better than wine.
verses.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for your love is better than wine.

verses.raw: Because of the savour of your good ointments your name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love you.
verses.text: Because of the savour of your good ointments your name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love you.

verses.raw: Draw me, we will run after you: the king has brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in you, we will remember your love more than wine: the upright love you.
verses.text: Draw me, we will run after you: the king has brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in you, we will remember your love more than wine: the upright love you.

verses.raw: I am black, but comely, O you daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
verses.text: I am black, but comely, O you daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

verses.raw: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun has looked upon me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but my own vineyard have I not kept.
verses.text: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun has looked upon me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but my own vineyard have I not kept.

verses.raw: Tell me, O you whom my soul loves, where you feedest, where you make your flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turns aside by the flocks of your companions?
verses.text: Tell me, O you whom my soul loves, where you feedest, where you make your flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turns aside by the flocks of your companions?

verses.raw: If you know not, O you fairest among women, go your way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed your kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
verses.text: If you know not, O you fairest among women, go your way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed your kids beside the shepherds’ tents.

verses.raw: I have compared you, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.
verses.text: I have compared you, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.

verses.raw: Your cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, your neck with chains of gold.
verses.text: Your cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, your neck with chains of gold.

verses.raw: We will make you borders of gold with studs of silver.
verses.text: We will make you borders of gold with studs of silver.

verses.raw: While the king sits at his table, my spikenard sends forth the smell thereof.
verses.text: While the king sits at his table, my spikenard sends forth the smell thereof.

verses.raw: A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
verses.text: A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

verses.raw: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.
verses.text: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.

verses.raw: Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves’ eyes.
verses.text: Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves’ eyes.

verses.raw: Behold, you are fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.
verses.text: Behold, you are fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.

verses.raw: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
verses.text: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.

verses.raw: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
verses.text: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.

verses.raw: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
verses.text: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

verses.raw: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.text: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

verses.raw: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
verses.text: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.

verses.raw: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
verses.text: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.

verses.raw: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand does embrace me.
verses.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand does embrace me.

verses.raw: I charge you, O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
verses.text: I charge you, O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

verses.raw: The voice of my beloved! behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
verses.text: The voice of my beloved! behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

verses.raw: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he stands behind our wall, he looks forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.
verses.text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he stands behind our wall, he looks forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.

verses.raw: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

verses.raw: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
verses.text: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;

verses.raw: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
verses.text: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

verses.raw: The fig tree puts forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.text: The fig tree puts forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

verses.raw: O my dove, that are in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see your countenance, let me hear your voice; for sweet is your voice, and your countenance is comely.
verses.text: O my dove, that are in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see your countenance, let me hear your voice; for sweet is your voice, and your countenance is comely.

verses.raw: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
verses.text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.

verses.raw: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
verses.text: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

verses.raw: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be you like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
verses.text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be you like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.

verses.raw: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.

verses.raw: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.text: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.

verses.raw: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw you him whom my soul loves?
verses.text: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw you him whom my soul loves?

verses.raw: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
verses.text: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

verses.raw: I charge you, O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
verses.text: I charge you, O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

verses.raw: Who is this that comes out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
verses.text: Who is this that comes out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

verses.raw: Behold his bed, which is Solomon’s; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Yashar'el (Israel).
verses.text: Behold his bed, which is Solomon’s; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Yashar'el.

verses.raw: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man has his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
verses.text: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man has his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

verses.raw: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
verses.text: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

verses.raw: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.text: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.raw: Go forth, O you daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.text: Go forth, O you daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

verses.raw: Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves’ eyes within your locks: your hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
verses.text: Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves’ eyes within your locks: your hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

verses.raw: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.
verses.text: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.

verses.raw: Your lips are like a thread of scarlet, and your speech is comely: your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within your locks.
verses.text: Your lips are like a thread of scarlet, and your speech is comely: your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within your locks.

verses.raw: Your neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
verses.text: Your neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

verses.raw: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
verses.text: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

verses.raw: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
verses.text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

verses.raw: You are all fair, my love; there is no spot in you.
verses.text: You are all fair, my love; there is no spot in you.

verses.raw: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
verses.text: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

verses.raw: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; you have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
verses.text: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; you have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.

verses.raw: How fair is your love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is your love than wine! and the smell of your ointments than all spices!
verses.text: How fair is your love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is your love than wine! and the smell of your ointments than all spices!

verses.raw: Your lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
verses.text: Your lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

verses.raw: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
verses.text: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

verses.raw: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
verses.text: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

verses.raw: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
verses.text: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

verses.raw: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
verses.text: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.

verses.raw: Awake, O north wind; and come, you south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
verses.text: Awake, O north wind; and come, you south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

verses.raw: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
verses.text: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

verses.raw: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocks, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
verses.text: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocks, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.

verses.raw: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
verses.text: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

verses.raw: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
verses.text: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.

verses.raw: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
verses.text: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

verses.raw: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
verses.text: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

verses.raw: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.text: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

verses.raw: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him, that I am sick of love.
verses.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him, that I am sick of love.

verses.raw: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O you fairest among women? what is your beloved more than another beloved, that you do so charge us?
verses.text: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O you fairest among women? what is your beloved more than another beloved, that you do so charge us?

verses.raw: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
verses.text: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.

verses.raw: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
verses.text: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

verses.raw: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
verses.text: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.

verses.raw: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
verses.text: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

verses.raw: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
verses.text: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

verses.raw: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.text: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

verses.raw: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.text: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.raw: Whither is your beloved gone, O you fairest among women? whither is your beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with you.
verses.text: Whither is your beloved gone, O you fairest among women? whither is your beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with you.

verses.raw: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

verses.raw: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
verses.text: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

verses.raw: You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
verses.text: You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.

verses.raw: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me: your hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
verses.text: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me: your hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

verses.raw: Your teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one bears twins, and there is not one barren among them.
verses.text: Your teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one bears twins, and there is not one barren among them.

verses.raw: As a piece of a pomegranate are your temples within your locks.
verses.text: As a piece of a pomegranate are your temples within your locks.

verses.raw: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
verses.text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

verses.raw: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
verses.text: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

verses.raw: Who is she that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
verses.text: Who is she that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?

verses.raw: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.
verses.text: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.

verses.raw: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
verses.text: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.

verses.raw: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon you. What will you see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
verses.text: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon you. What will you see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.

verses.raw: How beautiful are your feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
verses.text: How beautiful are your feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

verses.raw: Your navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: your belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
verses.text: Your navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: your belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.

verses.raw: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
verses.text: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.

verses.raw: Your neck is as a tower of ivory; your eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: your nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
verses.text: Your neck is as a tower of ivory; your eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: your nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.

verses.raw: Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.
verses.text: Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.

verses.raw: How fair and how pleasant are you, O love, for delights!
verses.text: How fair and how pleasant are you, O love, for delights!

verses.raw: This your stature is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters of grapes.
verses.text: This your stature is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters of grapes.

verses.raw: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also your breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of your nose like apples;
